handback.t:
Both findings are ADDRESSED. I found no new breakage in the fix diff.

**Finding 1 (chat read as a plugin message): ADDRESSED**
- `hooks/chat.ts:170` now calls `host.submitPrompt(message, { asUser: true })`.
- `hooks/host.ts` makes the signature `submitPrompt: (text, opts?: { asUser?: boolean }) => Promise<void>`.
- `hooks/register.ts:112-116` forwards `$.prompt.submit({ text, asUser: true })` only when `opts?.asUser === true`. Otherwise it makes the same `$.prompt.submit({ text })` call as before.

**Finding 2 (secret-shaped chat sent silently with screen off or 'unavailable'): ADDRESSED**
- `hooks/chat.ts:165` sets `screen` to `null` when the screen is off.
- `hooks/chat.ts:168` refuses with `NOT_SENT.pii` when `(screen === null || screen.status === 'unavailable') && hasSecret(message)`.
- Ordinary text still reaches the submit.
- `blocksGuidance(null)` is false (`mission-options.ts:120`), so the null path is typesafe.
- When the screen is on and `screen.status === 'pii'`, the refusal is chosen as before. The `screen?.status` change is behaviour-neutral.

**(a) Do the new tests bite? Yes, by reasoning against base 1b529a22a, plus one run at head.**
- "submits with asUser true" asserts `calls` equals `[['hello', { asUser: true }]]`. Base called `submitPrompt(message)` with one argument, so this fails there.
- "screen off + secret" asserts `submits` is empty and `chatOf(state).error` matches `/not sent/i`. Base skipped the whole `if` when the screen was off and submitted, so this fails there.
- "screen unavailable + secret" asserts the same. Base's `blocksGuidance` is false for 'unavailable', so it submitted and this fails there.
- "screen off + ordinary text submitted" is a regression guard. It passes on base and at head by design.
- "ask Claude keeps submitting without asUser" asserts one call with one argument. It passes on base too, which is correct for a guard.
- Run at head: `tests/chat-send.spec.ts` passes, 17 of 17.
- The no-echo test checks `JSON.stringify(chatOf(state))` for the key's middle characters.

**(b) Other `submitPrompt(` callers: unchanged, one argument each.**
- All in `hooks/`: `ap-live.ts:299`, `ask-claude.ts:166`, `loops.ts:177`, `help-actions.ts:68`, `mission-control.ts:357`, `:419`, `:480`, `mission-guidance.ts:92`, `mission-advisor-live.ts:47`, `mission-palette.ts:46`, `views/wf-templates.ts:111`.
- `data/wf-send.ts:148` calls `deps.submitPrompt(body)` with one argument, and the diff does not touch it.
- Only `chat.ts:170` passes `asUser`.

**(c) `hasSecret`: same dependency-free check as `model-tools`; the refusal does not echo the input.**
- `chat.ts` imports `hasSecret` from `./screen`, the same import `model-tools.ts:19` uses.
- `screen.ts:261` defines it as `hasSecretIn(SECRETS, text)`, a local rules check with no detector call.
- The refusal text is the fixed string `'not sent: AIDefence found personal or secret data in the message'`. It does not include the message.

**What `asUser` does, per `claude-code.d.ts` (`PromptSubmitArgs`, lines 8195-8214, and the origin type near 8147-8168)**
- The model reads the text bare, without the "The <plugin> plugin sent a message" frame.
- The origin every hook sees stays `{ kind: 'plugin', name, asUser: true }`, and the transcript still names the plugin.
- `prompt.submit` hooks and provenance gates still see it as a plugin origin, so nothing is bypassed. The d.ts says nothing about permission checks changing.
- `@file` mentions and pasted images are not expanded for a plugin's prompt, `asUser` or not.

**New breakage in the fix diff:** none.

**Out-of-scope observations**
- `chat.ts:125` JSDoc says "as a normal user turn". The transcript still attributes the turn to the plugin, which is fine but worth knowing.
- The "ask Claude" test reaches into `askActions` with `as never` casts. It is brittle but valid.

**Verdict: all findings addressed.**
